title: Find the top direction by products, then fit probabilistic PCA and factor analysis
brief: Read an eigenvalue with the Rayleigh quotient, find eigenvectors by multiplying and deflating, then write the E-step, the M-step, and the log-likelihood of probabilistic PCA and of factor analysis, which gives each column its own noise variance.
hints: rayleigh_quotient is one line: v @ A @ v / (v @ v).
power_iteration: start from np.ones(d) / np.sqrt(d), then loop `v = A @ v; v = v / np.linalg.norm(v)`. Rescale inside the loop, every step.
deflate: A - eigenvalue * np.outer(v, v). np.outer builds a (d, d) matrix; v @ v is only a number.
ppca_e_step: M_inv = np.linalg.inv(W.T @ W + sigma2 * np.eye(k)); Ez = Xc @ W @ M_inv; Ezz_sum = n * sigma2 * M_inv + Ez.T @ Ez.
ppca_m_step: W_new = (Xc.T @ Ez) @ np.linalg.inv(Ezz_sum). Then sigma2 = (sum(Xc**2) - 2 * sum(Ez * (Xc @ W_new)) + trace(Ezz_sum @ W_new.T @ W_new)) / (n * d), using W_new in every term.
ppca_loglik: C = W @ W.T + sigma2 * I, S = Xc.T @ Xc / n, then -0.5 * n * (d * log(2 pi) + slogdet(C)[1] + trace(solve(C, S))).
fa_e_step: P = W / psi[:, None]; M_inv = inv(I + W.T @ P); Ez = Xc @ P @ M_inv; Ezz_sum = n * M_inv + Ez.T @ Ez. Keep the n * M_inv term.
fa_m_step: cross = Xc.T @ Ez; W_new = cross @ inv(Ezz_sum); psi_new = (sum(Xc**2, axis=0) - sum(W_new * cross, axis=1)) / n, clipped at 1e-6. One value per column, not their average.
fa_loglik: the same as ppca_loglik with C = W @ W.T + np.diag(psi).
